key_insight: ENGINE couples low-variance subspace updates with high-dimensional corrections to improve zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning without additional peak memory overhead.
engineering_relevance: It transfers variational multiscale ideas from computational mechanics to memory-efficient optimization of large language models.
method: Treat low-dimensional and full parameter spaces as resolved coarse and unresolved fine scales.
Alternate between scales using a multigrid-style V-cycle.
Probe fine-scale information to correct coarse-space sampling and updates.
evidence_signal: On standard LLM benchmarks, the abstract reports higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing zeroth-order methods, with up to 2.61× speed-up measured in forward passes and zero additional peak memory overhead.
watch_item: Theoretical guarantees depend on assumptions, and forward-pass savings do not necessarily translate directly into wall-clock speed-ups.
paper_title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
